# Text decorations render at one immutable weight

## Symptom

Every decoration line this library draws over, through or under a text
object comes out at a single hard-coded visual weight. Consumers have no
way, through any public surface, to make those lines heavier or lighter.
The weight is identical for every text object, and identical for every
character inside a text object.

## Visual evidence

Reference renders of the intended result:

- `/app/.harbor_assets/design_ref_1.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/design_ref_2.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/design_ref_3.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/design_ref_4.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/design_ref_5.png`
- `/app/.harbor_assets/design_ref_6.png`

## Expected behaviour

Consumers can set the decoration line weight through the library's public
API, and the result matches the reference renders. The renders are
normative for the scope of the change: they show which of the decoration
lines drawn above, through and below the text the setting has to reach,
and how finely the weight is allowed to vary inside a single text object.

- The setting reaches every decoration line the renders show it reaching,
  not only one of them.
- The weight varies inside a single text object at the granularity the
  renders show, not only from one text object to the next.
- The setting survives the library's object round-trip: serialise a text
  object and rebuild it from that data, and the rebuilt object produces
  identical output.
- The setting is observable in the SVG the library emits, so that a
  rendered scene and its serialised SVG agree on the weight actually
  applied.
- The reported weight scales linearly with the setting: triple the
  setting and the weight reported in the emitted SVG triples.
- The weight in force today is the default. A consumer who never sets it
  sees exactly the text they see now, and explicitly setting the default
  is indistinguishable from not setting it at all.

content.text:
The implementation is complete. Here's what I did.

## Summary

The root cause: the decoration weight was the hard-coded literal `this.fontSize / 15`, repeated at all three `fillRect` call sites in `_renderTextDecoration` (covering underline, overline, and linethrough), with no public setting reaching it and no numeric weight in the exported SVG.

I added a public **`textDecorationThickness`** property — a multiplier on that base weight — wired through every surface the reference renders demand:

**Rendering (`Text.ts`)** — The three `this.fontSize / 15` sites now read `(this.fontSize / 15) * thickness`, where `thickness` comes from `getValueOfPropertyAt(i, j, 'textDecorationThickness')`. I added `currentThickness !== thickness` to the run-break condition so the weight can change **per character** within one text object (ref 5/6), not just per object. This reaches all three decoration lines (ref 5 shows over/through/under all varying).

**Default fidelity** — Default is `1`. Since `x * 1` is bit-identical in IEEE-754 and the historical weight already scaled with `fontSize`, a multiplier of `1` reproduces today's output exactly at every font size. A consumer who never sets it — or sets it to `1` explicitly — gets pixel-identical rendering and SVG.

**Serialization round-trip** — Registered in `additionalProps` (object-level `toObject`/`fromObject` + cache invalidation), `styleProperties` (per-character styles), and `StylePropertiesType`. Added to `hasStyleChanged`'s text-span branch so per-character values serialize into correct style ranges and rebuild identically.

**SVG (`TextSVGExportMixin.ts`)** — A new `getSvgTextDecorationThickness` emits `text-decoration-thickness` at the object level and `text-decoration-thickness: …px` at the span level, reporting the **actual rendered weight** (`fontSize/15 × thickness`). It's gated on a decoration being present, so decoration-free SVG is unchanged. Tripling the setting triples the emitted value (linear).

**Verification** — Added 3 durable tests (round-trip, all-three-lines + linear scaling, explicit-default indistinguishability), plus ad-hoc tests confirming canvas `fillRect` heights scale and vary per character. Updated the reference objects/snapshot/cache-property assertions that legitimately gained the new field. TypeScript is clean, the rollup build passes, and there are **zero net-new test failures** — the ~30 remaining failures are pre-existing node-canvas font-metric discrepancies present on the base commit, unaffected by this change.
